transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because things at work have gotten, I don’t know, too coordinated to ignore. I’m on this environmental modeling contract, and I’ve been going through revisions—datasets, model inputs, all the usual version iterations—and I’m pretty sure people involved with that contract have been tracking what I change. Not just reviewing it in the normal way, I mean following my revisions and then somehow planting errors into the datasets afterward so it looks like I’m the one making mistakes.

My wife keeps saying it’s probably version-control problems, and a couple of the junior analysts say the same thing, like, “Oh, it’s just a merge issue,” or “Someone opened the wrong file,” but I’ve done mathematical work long enough to know when errors are random and when they have a pattern. And the pattern is always that I look careless, or like I can’t lead the work. It’s hard to explain without showing you the files, but that’s why I’m here. I need someone to understand that this isn’t just me being upset about a few mistakes.
How long have you been noticing this pattern and feeling that people are deliberately tracking and sabotaging your work?

I’d say the point where I became really certain—where it stopped feeling like maybe I was just catching ordinary mistakes—was about two months ago. Before that there were little things, but I could explain them away, you know, because projects like this always have messy files and different versions floating around.

But for about the last two months, it’s been consistent enough that I can’t ignore it. That’s when I started feeling sure people on the project were tracking my revisions specifically, watching what I changed, and then errors would show up afterward in ways that made it look like I had introduced them. Not just once or twice—enough that it formed a pattern.
Besides these suspicions about your coworkers, have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things, that other people couldn't hear or see?

No, not really. I mean, I don’t hear voices talking to me or anything like that, if that’s what you mean. And I haven’t seen, you know, people or things that aren’t there.

Sometimes I’ll hear a noise in the office or at home and wonder what it was, but that’s normal, right? Like a computer fan, someone in the hallway, the house settling. I’m not saying I’m experiencing things other people can’t. My concern is more about the files and the pattern of changes. That’s the part that’s been hard to explain to people.

Before this situation at work started about two months ago, would you say you've generally been a trusting person in your relationships and past jobs, or have you often felt that people were out to deceive or undermine you throughout your life?

Before this? I mean… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve gone through life thinking everyone was trying to undermine me. I’ve worked with people for years, on contracts and teams, and sure, there are office politics sometimes, and people make mistakes or protect themselves, but I didn’t generally assume there was some deliberate effort against me.

That’s why this feels different. The certainty I’m talking about — that people on this project are tracking my revisions and then planting errors afterward — that’s really been there for about the last two months. Before that, I might notice odd things in a file and think, “Okay, that’s frustrating,” or “Someone used an old dataset,” but I wasn’t walking around my whole life believing people were out to get me. This became clear to me only recently, when the pattern kept repeating on this contract.

Aside from the concerns about your work files, have you noticed any changes in your day-to-day functioning—like your energy, motivation, personal hygiene, or your relationships with family and friends—since this all started?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed some changes, though I don’t know how much is from being worn down by the whole thing and how much is just me getting older or getting stuck in my own head.

I spend a lot more time just… sitting. Like I’ll be at my desk for hours, and it’s not even that I’m getting much done the whole time. Or I’ll go out to the garage where I keep my telescope, and it’s still covered, same as it was the last time. I used to really look forward to taking it out, going to astronomy nights, talking with people there about what we were looking at. Now I can know perfectly well that it’s something I used to enjoy, but I don’t feel that pull to actually start.

Same with hiking. I used to make plans, check the weather, pick a trail. Lately it feels like too much effort to even get ready. And with people… I’ve been less inclined to talk. I used to mentor some of the younger analysts and I liked that, explaining the math or walking them through how to think about a problem. Now even answering messages feels like something I put off.

So yes, I’d say my motivation and interest in things have dropped off. I’m still there, I’m still thinking, but it’s like the part of me that used to reach outward toward things is quieter.
Did you start feeling this drop in energy, interest, and motivation around the same time the concerns about your work files began, or did one come before the other?

It’s a little hard for me to separate cleanly, because when you’re in the middle of it, it doesn’t feel like one day everything changes. But if I really think about the timing, the broader drop-off started earlier than the last two months.

The decline — the energy being lower, the motivation not being what it used to be, pulling back from things — that really started after I was put in charge of the larger environmental modeling contract. That was about two years and two months ago. I remember it because it was supposed to be a step up, something I could handle, and at first I told myself I was just adjusting to the workload and the responsibility.

But after that, I started becoming more worn down and less engaged in things outside work. It wasn’t all at once. It was gradual. The concerns about the files became much clearer and more intense recently, but the loss of interest and motivation had already been creeping in since I took on that larger contract.
Over these past two years, have you noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, or any thoughts of not wanting to be alive?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I know you’re asking about the usual things people ask when someone seems run down, but I haven’t really kept a neat record of it in my head.

Sleep… some nights are worse than others, but I don’t know that I can say there’s been one obvious pattern. Appetite, I honestly haven’t paid that much attention to it. I eat because it’s time to eat, mostly. Concentration is hard to separate from the work itself, because if I’m staring at a model or a spreadsheet and something seems off, then of course my attention goes there and I can lose a lot of time checking it. But I don’t know if that’s “concentration trouble” in the way you mean.

As for guilt or worthlessness… I get frustrated with myself, sure. I think about how I used to be more on top of things and how I’m not moving through tasks the way I should. But I don’t know that I’d call it worthlessness exactly. And thoughts of not wanting to be alive—no, I don’t think of it that way. I get tired and discouraged, but I’m not sitting there planning anything or wanting to die.

Over these past two years, would you say this low mood and loss of interest has been fairly constant, present most days, or has it come and gone in more distinct episodes with periods where you felt more like your usual self?

I’d say it’s been more of a long decline than neat episodes. I don’t remember there being clear stretches where I suddenly felt like, “Oh, I’m back to myself now.” It’s more like after I was put in charge of that larger environmental modeling contract—about two years and two months ago—things started slipping, gradually.

At first I thought it was just the pressure of the contract, you know, the size of it, the responsibility, all the moving parts. But looking back, that’s really when this whole change began. Since then it’s been kind of… persistent. Some days are a little better than others, sure, but I wouldn’t describe it as coming and going in separate episodes. More like a steady lowering of where my normal baseline is.

If a colleague showed you clear technical evidence—like system logs—that no one had actually altered your files, do you think that would change your mind, or would you still feel convinced they were responsible?

I mean… I would look at the logs, of course. I’m not saying I would refuse to look at something technical. That’s my work — I understand audit trails and revision histories and how these systems can make things look one way or another.

But I don’t think a log by itself would settle it for me, no. Because if someone is tracking my revisions and knows when I’m making changes, then the whole point would be to make it look like ordinary version-control mistakes or bad handoffs between analysts. That’s exactly what my wife says, and some of the junior analysts have said it too — that I’m reading too much into routine file issues. But the pattern doesn’t feel routine to me.

It’s not just one file being off one time. It’s the way errors appear in datasets after I’ve worked through them, or after I’ve made a correction and then later something looks wrong again, like it’s been planted there so it comes back on me. And with this environmental modeling contract, if I look incompetent leading it, that benefits certain people. So if a colleague came in with logs saying, “See, no one altered anything,” I’d want to know who generated those logs, who had access before that, whether the logs themselves could have missed something.

So… would it change my mind? Maybe it would make me pause, depending on how complete it was. But honestly, I’d still be very suspicious. I don’t think I could just say, “Okay, then nobody did anything.” It feels too coordinated for that.

Aside from this situation with the work files, have you found yourself suspicious or distrustful of other people in your life—like family, friends, or people you don't know well—or is this feeling of being targeted really limited to the people connected to this contract?

It’s mostly tied to the contract, I think. I don’t walk around thinking every stranger is part of something, if that’s what you mean. Like if someone at the grocery store looks at me funny, I’m not building a whole theory around that.

But with the people connected to the environmental modeling work, it’s different, because there’s an actual trail of things happening. The revisions, the datasets, errors showing up where they shouldn’t be showing up. It isn’t just a vague feeling that people don’t like me. It’s specifically that people on or around that contract have been tracking what I change and then planting mistakes in the files so it looks like I can’t handle leading the work.

My wife keeps saying it’s version-control issues or that the junior analysts are just making normal mistakes, and some of them say the same thing, like I’m overreading it. But that doesn’t fit what I’m seeing. Not to me. So no, I wouldn’t say I’m broadly suspicious of everyone in my life. It’s really centered on the people who have access to that work and would benefit if I looked incompetent.

Aside from this specific situation with the contract files, would you say you're still able to function normally in other areas of your job and home life—like managing other projects, doing daily tasks, or interacting with people—or has this belief affected your functioning more broadly?

It’s affected more than just the files, yes. I mean, I’d like to say I’m keeping the rest of it separate, because that’s what I’ve always done—I’ve always been able to compartmentalize work problems and still get the math done, still manage people, still keep the household stuff moving. But lately… no, I don’t think that’s true anymore.

On the modeling deliverables, I’ve fallen far enough behind that the firm started reassigning pieces of the contract. Not the whole thing, but enough that it was obvious. Parts I was supposed to be coordinating got moved to other people because I wasn’t getting them out cleanly or on time. And that’s humiliating, honestly, because I’m supposed to be the one keeping the technical pieces straight.

And with the junior analysts, I’m not much use to them right now. I’m supposed to review their work, answer questions, help them understand why a model output looks wrong or how to structure the datasets, but I get stuck going back through things, checking whether something has changed, trying to trace where mistakes came from. So when they come to me, I’m either distracted or I give them half an answer and then circle back later. I can tell they’ve stopped relying on me the way they used to.

At home it’s quieter, but not in a good way. I mostly keep to myself. I sit with my notes or my laptop, or I just sort of stay in my own head. My wife has to push me to keep basic routines going—meals, laundry, getting out of the house, normal things. I still do some of it, but it’s not automatic anymore. If she didn’t nudge me, I’d probably let more of it slide. So… yes, it’s broader than just one work issue now.

patient.answer:
Well… I’m here because things at work have gotten, I don’t know, too coordinated to ignore. I’m on this environmental modeling contract, and I’ve been going through revisions—datasets, model inputs, all the usual version iterations—and I’m pretty sure people involved with that contract have been tracking what I change. Not just reviewing it in the normal way, I mean following my revisions and then somehow planting errors into the datasets afterward so it looks like I’m the one making mistakes.

My wife keeps saying it’s probably version-control problems, and a couple of the junior analysts say the same thing, like, “Oh, it’s just a merge issue,” or “Someone opened the wrong file,” but I’ve done mathematical work long enough to know when errors are random and when they have a pattern. And the pattern is always that I look careless, or like I can’t lead the work. It’s hard to explain without showing you the files, but that’s why I’m here. I need someone to understand that this isn’t just me being upset about a few mistakes.
